verses.text: Many tried to set down story of things fulfilled among us,
handed down by eyewitnesses and ministers of Word.
It seemed good to me too, having tracked all from start, to write orderly to you, most excellent Theophilus,
so you know certainty of what you’ve been taught.
In days of Herod king of Judea, there was priest Zacharias of Abijah division, wife Elisabeth of Aaron’s daughters.
They were righteous before God, walking blameless in commandments.
They had no child, Elisabeth barren, both old.
While Zacharias served as priest before God,
his lot fell to burn incense in temple.
Whole crowd prayed outside at incense hour.
Angel of Lord appeared to him, standing right side of altar.
Zacharias was shook, fear hit him.
Angel said: “Don’t fear, your prayer heard. Your wife Elisabeth will bear son, call him John.
You’ll have joy, many rejoice at his birth.
He’ll be great before Lord, won’t drink wine or strong drink, filled with Holy Spirit from womb.
He’ll turn many of Israel to Lord their God.
He’ll go before Him in spirit and power of Elijah, turn hearts of fathers to children, disobedient to wisdom of just, to prep people for Lord.”
Zacharias said: “How can I know? I’m old, my wife old.”
Angel said: “I’m Gabriel, stand in God’s presence, sent to speak, bring good news.
You’ll be mute, not speak till these things happen, cuz you didn’t believe.”
People waited, wondered why he delayed in temple.
When he came out, he couldn’t speak. They realized he saw vision. He beckoned, remained mute.
When his service ended, he went home.
After those days Elisabeth conceived, hid herself five months:
“Lord looked on me, took away my reproach.”
Sixth month, angel Gabriel sent from God to Nazareth, Galilee,
to virgin engaged to man named Joseph, of David’s house. Virgin’s name Mary.
Angel came: “Hail, favored one, Lord with you, blessed among women.”
She was troubled, wondered what greeting meant.
Angel said: “Don’t fear, Mary, you found favor with God.
You’ll conceive, bear son, call Him Jesus.
He’ll be great, called Son of Highest. Lord God will give Him throne of David.
He’ll reign over Jacob’s house forever, kingdom no end.”
Mary said: “How, since I don’t know man?”
Angel said: “Holy Spirit will come, power of Highest overshadow. Holy One born will be called Son of God.
Your cousin Elisabeth conceived son in old age, sixth month for her who was called barren.
With God nothing impossible.”
Mary said: “I’m Lord’s servant. Let it be.” Angel left.
Mary arose, went into hill country, to city of Judah,
entered Zacharias’ house, greeted Elisabeth.
When Elisabeth heard, baby leaped in womb, she was filled with Holy Spirit.
She cried: “Blessed are you among women, blessed is fruit of your womb.
Why is this granted to me, mother of my Lord comes?
As soon as your greeting sounded, baby leaped for joy.
Blessed is she who believed, for what Lord spoken will be fulfilled.”
Mary said: “My soul magnifies Lord,
my spirit rejoices in God my Savior.
He looked on low estate of His servant. From now all generations call me blessed.
Mighty One did great things for me, holy is His name.
His mercy on those who fear Him from generation to generation.
He showed strength, scattered proud in heart.
He put down mighty, exalted lowly.
He filled hungry with good, sent rich away empty.
He helped His servant Israel, remembering mercy,
as He spoke to fathers, to Abraham and his seed forever.”
Mary stayed three months, returned home.
Elisabeth’s time came, she delivered son.
Neighbors and kin rejoiced with her.
On eighth day they came to circumcise child, called him Zacharias after father.
Mother said: “No, he’ll be called John.”
They said: “None of your kin called that.”
They made signs to father what he wanted.
He asked for writing tablet, wrote: “His name is John.” They marveled.
His mouth opened, tongue loosed, he spoke, praised God.
Fear came on neighbors, word spread through Judea.
All who heard laid it up: “What will this child be?” Hand of Lord with him.
His father Zacharias filled with Holy Spirit, prophesied:
“Blessed be Lord God of Israel, He visited, redeemed His people,
raised horn of salvation in house of David,
as He spoke by prophets.
Salvation from enemies, from all who hate us.
Mercy promised to fathers, remember holy covenant,
oath to Abraham,
grant us delivered from enemies to serve Him without fear,
in holiness and righteousness before Him all our days.
You, child, will be called prophet of Highest, go before Lord to prepare His ways,
give knowledge of salvation to His people by forgiveness of sins,
through tender mercy of God, whereby sunrise from on high visited us,
to give light to those in darkness, shadow of death, guide feet into way of peace.”
Child grew, became strong in spirit, lived in wilderness till day of showing to Israel.
In those days Caesar Augustus dropped a decree: all world should be taxed.
This was first census when Cyrenius was governor of Syria.
Everyone went to their own city to register.
Joseph went up from Galilee, out of Nazareth, to Judea, city of David called Bethlehem, cuz he was of David’s line.
He went with Mary his engaged wife, who was pregnant.
While they were there, time came for her to deliver.
She gave birth to her firstborn son, wrapped Him in swaddling clothes, laid Him in manger, cuz no room in inn.
Shepherds were in fields nearby, keeping watch over flock at night.
Angel of Lord came, glory of Lord shone, they were shook.
Angel said: “Don’t fear. I bring good news of great joy for all people.
Today in city of David a Savior is born, Christ the Lord.
This is sign: You’ll find baby wrapped, lying in manger.”
Suddenly with angel a multitude of heavenly host praising God:
“Glory to God in highest, peace on earth, goodwill to men.”
When angels left, shepherds said: “Let’s go to Bethlehem, see this thing Lord made known.”
They came quick, found Mary, Joseph, and baby lying in manger.
When they saw, they spread word about what was told concerning child.
All who heard marveled at what shepherds said.
Mary kept all these things, pondered in heart.
Shepherds returned, glorifying, praising God for all they heard and saw.
When eight days were done, child circumcised, called Jesus, name given by angel before conception.
When days of purification were done, they brought Him to Jerusalem to present to Lord.
As written: Every male that opens womb shall be called holy to Lord.
They offered sacrifice: pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.
In Jerusalem was man Simeon, just and devout, waiting for consolation of Israel. Holy Spirit on him.
Spirit revealed he wouldn’t see death before seeing Lord’s Christ.
He came by Spirit into temple. When parents brought child Jesus to do custom,
Simeon took Him, blessed God:
“Lord, now let Your servant depart in peace, according to Your word.
My eyes have seen Your salvation,
prepared before all people,
light to Gentiles, glory of Israel.”
Joseph and mother marveled at things spoken.
Simeon blessed them, said to Mary: “This child set for fall and rising of many in Israel, sign spoken against.
A sword will pierce your soul also, that thoughts of many hearts revealed.”
There was Anna, prophetess, daughter of Phanuel, tribe of Asher, very old, lived with husband seven years, then widow till 84.
She didn’t leave temple, served God with fastings and prayers night and day.
She came in that instant, gave thanks, spoke of Him to all waiting for redemption in Jerusalem.
When they finished all according to law, they returned to Galilee, Nazareth.
Child grew, waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom, God’s favor on Him.
Every year His parents went to Jerusalem for Passover.
When He was twelve, they went up after custom.
When days were done, they returned, child Jesus stayed in Jerusalem, Joseph and mother didn’t know.
Thinking He was in company, they went a day’s journey, sought Him among kin.
When they didn’t find Him, they returned to Jerusalem seeking.
After three days they found Him in temple, sitting among teachers, listening, asking questions.
All who heard Him were amazed at His understanding and answers.
When parents saw Him, they were astonished. Mother said: “Son, why did You do this? We sought You sorrowing.”
He said: “Why did you seek Me? Didn’t you know I must be about My Father’s business?”
They didn’t understand His saying.
He went down with them, came to Nazareth, was subject to them. Mother kept sayings in heart.
Jesus grew in wisdom, stature, favor with God and men.
In fifteenth year of reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate governor of Judea, Herod tetrarch of Galilee, Philip tetrarch of Ituraea and Trachonitis, Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,
Annas and Caiaphas were high priests. Word of God came to John son of Zacharias in wilderness.
He went through all Jordan region, preaching baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.
As written in Isaiah: “Voice crying in wilderness: Prepare way of Lord, make paths straight.
Every valley filled, mountain and hill brought low, crooked straight, rough smooth.
All flesh shall see salvation of God.”
He said to crowds coming to be baptized: “Brood of vipers, who warned you to flee wrath?
Bring fruits worthy of repentance. Don’t say: We have Abraham as father. God can raise children to Abraham from stones.
Axe laid to root of trees. Every tree not bearing good fruit cut down, thrown into fire.”
Crowd asked: “What should we do?”
He said: “Whoever has two coats, share with one who has none. Same with food.”
Tax collectors came: “Master, what should we do?”
He said: “Collect no more than appointed.”
Soldiers asked: “What about us?” He said: “Don’t extort, don’t accuse falsely, be content with wages.”
People waited, wondered if John was Christ.
John said: “I baptize with water, but One mightier comes, straps I’m not worthy to untie. He’ll baptize with Holy Spirit and fire.
His fan in His hand, He’ll purge floor, gather wheat, burn chaff with fire unquenchable.”
With many other exhortations he preached.
But Herod the tetrarch, reproved by him for Herodias his brother’s wife and all evils,
added this: he locked John in prison.
When all people were baptized, Jesus also baptized, praying, heaven opened,
Holy Spirit descended like dove, voice from heaven: “You are My beloved Son, in You I’m well pleased.”
Jesus Himself began ministry at about thirty years old, being (as supposed) son of Joseph, son of Heli,
son of Matthat, son of Levi, son of Melchi, son of Janna, son of Joseph,
son of Mattathias, son of Amos, son of Naum, son of Esli, son of Nagge,
son of Maath, son of Mattathias, son of Semei, son of Joseph, son of Juda,
son of Joanna, son of Rhesa, son of Zorobabel, son of Salathiel, son of Neri,
son of Melchi, son of Addi, son of Cosam, son of Elmodam, son of Er,
son of Jose, son of Eliezer, son of Jorim, son of Matthat, son of Levi,
son of Simeon, son of Juda, son of Joseph, son of Jonan, son of Eliakim,
son of Melea, son of Menan, son of Mattatha, son of Nathan, son of David,
son of Jesse, son of Obed, son of Booz, son of Salmon, son of Naasson,
son of Aminadab, son of Aram, son of Esrom, son of Phares, son of Juda,
son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, son of Thara, son of Nachor,
son of Saruch, son of Ragau, son of Phalec, son of Heber, son of Sala,
son of Cainan, son of Arphaxad, son of Sem, son of Noe, son of Lamech,
son of Mathusala, son of Enoch, son of Jared, son of Maleleel, son of Cainan,
son of Enos, son of Seth, son of Adam, son of God.
Jesus, full of Holy Spirit, returned from Jordan, was led by Spirit into wilderness.
Forty days tempted by devil. He ate nothing, afterward hungry.
Devil said: “If You Son of God, command stone become bread.”
Jesus said: “It’s written, man shall not live by bread alone, but by God’s Word.”
Devil took Him up, showed all kingdoms in moment.
Said: “All power, glory delivered to me, I give to whoever.
If You worship me, all Yours.”
Jesus said: “Get behind me, Satan. It’s written, worship Lord your God, serve Him only.”
Devil brought Him to Jerusalem, set Him on temple pinnacle: “If You Son of God, throw Yourself down.
It’s written, He’ll give angels charge over You,
they’ll guard You, lift You up, lest You dash foot.”
Jesus said: “It’s written, don’t test Lord your God.”
Devil ended temptation, departed till another time.
Jesus returned in Spirit’s power to Galilee, fame spread.
He taught in synagogues, glorified by all.
He came to Nazareth where He grew up, went into synagogue on Sabbath, stood to read.
Book of Isaiah given. He opened, found place:
“Spirit of Lord on Me, He anointed Me to preach gospel to poor, sent Me to heal brokenhearted, proclaim liberty to captives, recovery of sight to blind, set free oppressed,
proclaim acceptable year of Lord.”
He closed book, gave to minister, sat. Eyes of all fixed on Him.
He said: “Today this scripture fulfilled in your ears.”
All bore witness, marveled at gracious words: “Isn’t this Joseph’s son?”
He said: “You’ll surely say, Physician, heal Yourself. Do here what we heard You did in Capernaum.”
He said: “No prophet accepted in his own country.
Truth: many widows in Israel in Elijah’s days when heaven shut three years six months, famine hit.
Elijah sent to none but widow in Zarephath, Sidon.
Many lepers in Israel in Elisha’s time, none cleansed except Naaman Syrian.”
All in synagogue hearing this were mad.
They rose, drove Him out, led Him to hill to throw Him down.
But He passed through middle, went His way.
He came to Capernaum, Galilee, taught on Sabbath.
They were astonished at His teaching, His word had authority.
In synagogue was man with unclean demon spirit. He cried:
“Let us alone! What have we to do with You, Jesus of Nazareth? Did You come to destroy us? I know You, Holy One of God.”
Jesus rebuked: “Be quiet, come out.” Demon threw him down, came out, didn’t hurt him.
All amazed: “What word is this? With authority and power He commands unclean spirits, they come out.”
Fame spread everywhere.
He arose, entered Simon’s house. Simon’s mother-in-law sick with fever. They asked Him for her.
He stood over her, rebuked fever, it left. She rose, served them.
When sun set, all with sick brought them. He laid hands, healed them.
Demons came out of many, crying: “You are Christ, Son of God.” He rebuked, didn’t allow them to speak, cuz they knew He was Christ.
Morning, He departed to solitary place. Crowd sought Him, tried to keep Him from leaving.
He said: “I must preach kingdom of God to other cities also, for this purpose I was sent.”
He preached in synagogues of Galilee.
Crowd pressed on Him to hear Word of God, He stood by Lake of Gennesaret.
He saw two boats by lake, fishermen gone, washing nets.
He entered one boat, Simon’s, asked him to push out a little. He sat, taught crowd from boat.
When He finished, He said to Simon: “Launch into deep, let down nets for catch.”
Simon said: “Master, we worked all night, caught nothing. But at Your word, I’ll let down net.”
When they did, they caught huge number of fish, net breaking.
They signaled partners in other boat to help. They came, filled both boats, so they began to sink.
Simon Peter saw, fell at Jesus’ knees: “Lord, depart from me, I’m sinful man.”
He and all with him were astonished at catch.
James and John, sons of Zebedee, partners with Simon, were also amazed. Jesus said: “Don’t fear. From now you’ll catch men.”
They brought boats to land, left all, followed Him.
In one city, a man full of leprosy saw Jesus, fell on face: “Lord, if You will, You can make me clean.”
Jesus stretched hand, touched him: “I will, be clean.” Immediately leprosy left.
He charged him: “Tell no one, but go show yourself to priest, offer gift Moses commanded.”
Fame spread, crowds came to hear, be healed.
He withdrew to wilderness, prayed.
One day He taught, Pharisees and doctors of law sat by, from every village of Galilee, Judea, Jerusalem. Power of Lord present to heal.
Men brought a paralyzed man on bed, sought to bring him in, lay before Him.
Finding no way cuz of crowd, they went up roof, lowered him with bed through tiles into midst before Jesus.
Seeing their faith, He said: “Man, your sins forgiven.”
Scribes and Pharisees thought: “Who is this speaking blasphemies? Who can forgive sins but God?”
Jesus perceived thoughts: “Why reason in hearts?
Which easier, say: Your sins forgiven, or say: Rise and walk?
But so you know Son of Man has authority to forgive sins—He said to paralyzed man: Rise, take bed, go home.”
Immediately he rose, took bed, went home glorifying God.
All were amazed, glorified God, filled with fear: “We saw strange things today.”
After, He went out, saw Levi (Matthew) sitting at tax booth, said: “Follow Me.” He left all, followed.
Levi made Him great feast at his house. Many tax collectors and others sat with them.
Scribes and Pharisees murmured: “Why eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus said: “They that are whole need no physician, but sick do.
I came not to call righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
They said: “Why do John’s disciples fast often, make prayers, likewise Pharisees, but Yours eat and drink?”
He said: “Can you make wedding guests fast while bridegroom with them?
Days will come when bridegroom taken, then they’ll fast.”
He spoke parable: “No one puts new patch on old garment, else new tears, old doesn’t match.
No one puts new wine in old skins, else skins burst, wine spilled, skins ruined.
New wine must be put in new skins.
No one drinking old wine immediately desires new, for he says, old is better.”
One Sabbath, Jesus and His crew walked through grain fields. They plucked heads of grain, rubbed them, ate.
Some Pharisees said: “Why y’all doing what’s not lawful on Sabbath?”
Jesus said: “Haven’t you read what David did when hungry—he and his squad?
He went into house of God, ate showbread, which only priests can eat, gave to his guys too.”
He said: “Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
On another Sabbath, He entered synagogue, taught. A man was there with a withered hand.
Scribes and Pharisees watched to see if He’d heal on Sabbath so they could accuse Him.
He knew their thoughts. He said to the man: “Rise, stand in the middle.” He stood.
Jesus said: “I ask you—is it lawful on Sabbath to do good or evil, save life or destroy?”
He looked around at them all, said to man: “Stretch out your hand.” He did, and it was restored.
They were filled with rage, discussed what to do to Jesus.
In those days He went to mountain to pray, stayed all night praying to God.
When day came, He called disciples, chose twelve, called them apostles:
Simon (He named Peter), Andrew his brother, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew,
Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Simon called Zealot,
Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became traitor.
He came down with them, stood in plain. Big crowd of disciples and people from all Judea, Jerusalem, Tyre, Sidon came to hear and be healed.
Those with unclean spirits were healed.
Whole crowd tried to touch Him—power came from Him, healed all.
He lifted His eyes to disciples: “Blessed are you poor, for yours is kingdom of God.
Blessed are you hungry now, you’ll be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, you’ll laugh.
Blessed are you when people hate you, exclude you, insult you, reject your name as evil for Son of Man’s sake.
Rejoice in that day, leap for joy! Your reward is great in heaven. That’s how their ancestors treated prophets.”
“But woe to you rich—you’ve had your comfort.
Woe to you full—you’ll be hungry. Woe to you laughing now—you’ll mourn and weep.
Woe when everyone speaks well of you—that’s how they hyped false prophets.”
“But I say to you who hear: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you.
Bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.
If someone hits your cheek, offer the other. If they take your coat, don’t stop them from taking your shirt.
Give to everyone who asks. If someone takes what’s yours, don’t demand it back.
Do to others what you want them to do to you.”
“If you love those who love you, what credit is that? Even sinners do that.
If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that? Sinners do the same.
If you lend to those you expect to repay, what credit is that? Sinners lend to get back full.
But love your enemies, do good, lend expecting nothing back. Your reward will be great, and you’ll be children of the Highest. He’s kind to unthankful and evil.
Be merciful, just like your Father is merciful.”
“Don’t judge, and you won’t be judged. Don’t condemn, and you won’t be condemned. Forgive, and you’ll be forgiven.
Give, and it’ll be given to you—good measure, pressed down, shaken together, running over. With the measure you use, it’ll be measured back.”
He told a parable: “Can the blind lead the blind? Won’t they both fall in ditch?
A disciple isn’t above teacher, but everyone fully trained will be like teacher.
Why look at speck in your brother’s eye but ignore plank in your own?
How can you say, ‘Let me take out your speck,’ when you don’t see the plank in your own? Hypocrite! First remove plank from your eye, then you’ll see clearly to help your brother.”
“A good tree doesn’t bear bad fruit, nor a bad tree good fruit.
Every tree known by its fruit. You don’t gather figs from thorns or grapes from brambles.
A good person brings good from good heart. Evil brings evil from evil heart. Out of heart’s overflow, mouth speaks.”
“Why call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and not do what I say?
Whoever comes to Me, hears My words, and does them—I’ll show you what they’re like.
Like a man building house, dug deep, laid foundation on rock. When flood came, stream beat on house, couldn’t shake it—it was built solid.
But one who hears and doesn’t do is like man who built house on ground without foundation. Stream hit it, and it collapsed instantly.”
When Jesus finished all His sayings to the people, He dipped from the mic and entered Capernaum.
A centurion had a servant, sick and near death—dude was mad valuable to him.
When he heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to ask Him to come heal the servant.
They came to Jesus, begged hard: “He deserves this—
he loves our nation, even built us a synagogue.”
Jesus went with them. When He was close to the house, the centurion sent friends: “Lord, don’t trouble Yourself. I’m not worthy You should enter my crib.
That’s why I didn’t come myself. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
I’m a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I say ‘Go,’ and they go; ‘Come,’ and they come; ‘Do this,’ and it’s done.”
Jesus heard, marveled, turned to the crowd: “I haven’t found faith like this even in Israel.”
Those sent returned to the house, found the servant healed.
Soon after, He went to a town called Nain. His disciples and a big crowd rolled with Him.
As He neared the gate, a dead man was being carried out—only son of a widow. A large crowd was with her.
When Jesus saw her, He was moved: “Don’t cry.”
He touched the coffin. The carriers stopped. He said: “Young man, I say to you, rise.”
The dead sat up and spoke. Jesus gave him back to his mom.
Everyone was shook, glorified God: “A great prophet has risen!” and “God has visited His people!”
This news spread all over Judea and the surrounding region.
John’s disciples told him all this. He called two of them,
sent them to Jesus: “Are You the One, or should we wait for another?”
They came: “John the Baptist sent us to ask—are You the One?”
That same hour, Jesus healed many of diseases, plagues, evil spirits, and gave sight to the blind.
He answered: “Go tell John what you’ve seen and heard: the blind see, lame walk, lepers cleansed, deaf hear, dead raised, and the gospel preached to the poor.
Blessed is anyone who doesn’t trip over Me.”
When John’s messengers left, Jesus spoke to the crowd: “What’d y’all go out to the wilderness to see? A reed shaking in the wind?
A man in soft clothes? Nah, those live in palaces.
You went to see a prophet? Facts. And more than a prophet.
This is the one the scripture spoke of: ‘I send My messenger before You, who’ll prep Your path.’
I tell you, among those born of women, none greater than John. But even the least in God’s kingdom is greater than him.”
All the people, even tax collectors, justified God, having been baptized by John.
But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected God’s purpose, refusing John’s baptism.
Jesus said: “To what shall I compare this generation?
They’re like kids in the market yelling, ‘We played the flute, you didn’t dance. We mourned, you didn’t cry.’
John came fasting, no wine, and y’all said, ‘He’s got a demon.’
Son of Man came eating and drinking, and y’all say, ‘Look, a glutton and drunk, friend of tax collectors and sinners!’
But wisdom is proven right by her children.”
One of the Pharisees invited Him to eat. Jesus went to his house, sat down.
A woman in the city, known as a sinner, heard He was there. She brought an alabaster jar of perfume.
She stood behind Him, weeping, washed His feet with her tears, wiped them with her hair, kissed them, and anointed them.
The Pharisee thought: “If He were a prophet, He’d know what kind of woman this is—she’s a sinner.”
Jesus said: “Simon, I got something to say.” He said: “Say it, Teacher.”
“A lender had two debtors. One owed 500 silver coins, the other 50.
Neither could pay. He forgave both. Who’ll love him more?”
Simon said: “The one forgiven more.” Jesus said: “You judged right.”
He turned to the woman: “See her? I entered your house, you gave no water for My feet—she washed them with tears.
You gave no kiss—she hasn’t stopped kissing My feet.
You didn’t anoint My head—she poured perfume on My feet.
So I tell you, her many sins are forgiven—she loved much. But whoever’s forgiven little, loves little.”
He said to her: “Your sins are forgiven.”
Those at the table said: “Who is this who forgives sins?”
He said to the woman: “Your faith saved you. Go in peace.”
Jesus went city to city, village to village, preaching good news of God’s kingdom. The twelve were with Him,
and some women He’d healed of evil spirits and sickness: Mary Magdalene (seven demons cast out),
Joanna (wife of Chuza, Herod’s steward), Susanna, and many others who supported Him with their own money.
When a massive crowd gathered from town after town, He dropped this parable:
“A sower went out to plant seed. Some fell by the road, got stepped on, birds ate it.
Some fell on rocks—sprouted, but withered cuz no moisture.
Some fell among thorns—thorns grew up and choked it.
Some fell on good ground—grew, produced a hundredfold.” He shouted, “Whoever got ears, listen up!”
Disciples asked what the parable meant.
He said: “You get the secrets of God’s kingdom. But to others, it’s parables—so seeing they don’t see, hearing they don’t understand.”
“The seed is God’s Word.
Those by the road hear, but then the devil snatches the word so they don’t believe and get saved.
On the rock—those hear with joy, but no roots. They believe for a bit, then fall off when tested.
Among thorns—those hear, but get choked by life’s worries, riches, and pleasures. No fruit.
Good ground—those with honest, good hearts hear, hold it down, and bear fruit with patience.”
“No one lights a lamp and hides it or puts it under a bed. They put it on a stand so others see the light.
Nothing hidden won’t be revealed. Nothing secret won’t be known and brought to light.
So watch how you hear. Whoever has, more will be given. Whoever doesn’t, even what they think they have will be taken.”
His mom and brothers came but couldn’t reach Him cuz of the crowd.
Someone said: “Your mother and brothers are outside, wanting to see You.”
He said: “My mother and brothers are those who hear God’s Word and do it.”
One day He got in a boat with disciples: “Let’s cross the lake.” They launched.
As they sailed, He fell asleep. A storm hit, waves filled the boat. They were in danger.
They woke Him: “Master, we’re dying!” He got up, rebuked wind and waves—they calmed. He said: “Where’s your faith?”
They were shook: “Who is this? Even wind and water obey Him!”
They sailed to Gerasenes, across from Galilee.
When He stepped ashore, a demon-possessed man met Him—naked, living in tombs.
He screamed, fell before Jesus: “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? Don’t torture me!”
(Jesus had commanded the unclean spirit to come out. It had often seized him—he was chained, but broke free and was driven into the wild.)
Jesus asked: “What’s your name?” He said: “Legion”—many demons had entered him.
They begged Him not to send them into the abyss.
A herd of pigs was feeding nearby. They begged to enter the pigs. He let them.
The demons left the man, entered pigs—the herd rushed down a cliff into the lake and drowned.
The herders saw it, ran and told the town and countryside.
People came, found the man sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed, sane. They were terrified.
Witnesses told how the demon-possessed man was healed.
Whole region begged Jesus to leave—they were overwhelmed with fear. He got in the boat and left.
The man begged to go with Him. Jesus said:
“Go home. Tell what God’s done for you.” He went through the city, shouting what Jesus had done.
When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed Him—they’d been waiting.
A man named Jairus, synagogue leader, came, fell at Jesus’ feet: “Come to my house.
My only daughter, about twelve, is dying.” As Jesus went, the crowd pressed in.
A woman with a 12-year bleeding issue, who’d spent all her money on doctors with no cure,
came behind Him, touched the edge of His cloak—and instantly the bleeding stopped.
Jesus said: “Who touched Me?” Everyone denied. Peter said: “Master, the crowd’s all over You.”
Jesus said: “Someone touched Me—I felt power go out.”
The woman, realizing she couldn’t hide, came trembling, fell before Him, told why she touched Him and how she was healed.
He said: “Daughter, your faith healed you. Go in peace.”
While He spoke, someone from Jairus’s house came: “Your daughter’s dead. Don’t bother the Teacher.”
Jesus said: “Don’t fear. Just believe, and she’ll be healed.”
He came to the house, let no one in but Peter, James, John, and the girl’s parents.
People were weeping. He said: “Stop crying. She’s not dead, just sleeping.”
They laughed at Him—they knew she was dead.
He took her hand: “Little girl, get up.”
Her spirit returned, she got up immediately. He told them to give her food.
Her parents were amazed. He told them not to tell anyone what happened.
Jesus called the twelve, gave them power and authority over all demons and to heal diseases.
He sent them to preach God’s kingdom and heal the sick.
He said: “Take nothing—no staff, bag, bread, money, or extra shirt.
Stay in whatever house you enter till you leave that town.
If they don’t receive you, shake the dust off your feet as a witness when you bounce.”
They went out, hit up villages, preaching and healing everywhere.
Herod the tetrarch heard all that was happening. He was confused—some said John was raised from the dead,
others said Elijah appeared, or a prophet from the past had risen.
Herod said: “I beheaded John. Who is this I’m hearing about?” He wanted to see Jesus.
The apostles returned, told Jesus everything. He took them privately to a town called Bethsaida.
But the crowd found out and followed. He welcomed them, spoke about God’s kingdom, healed those in need.
Late in the day, the twelve said: “Send the crowd away to nearby towns for food and lodging—we’re in the middle of nowhere.”
Jesus said: “You give them something to eat.” They said: “We only got five loaves and two fish—unless we go buy food for all.”
There were about 5,000 men. He said: “Have them sit in groups of fifty.”
They did. Everyone sat down.
He took the five loaves and two fish, looked up, blessed them, broke them, gave to disciples to set before the crowd.
They all ate and were filled. Twelve baskets of leftovers were picked up.
While He was praying alone, His disciples were with Him. He asked: “Who do the crowds say I am?”
They said: “John the Baptist. Others say Elijah. Others say a prophet from long ago.”
He said: “But who do you say I am?” Peter answered: “You’re the Christ of God.”
He warned them not to tell anyone.
He said: “Son of Man must suffer, be rejected by elders, priests, scribes, be killed, and rise on the third day.”
He said to all: “If anyone wants to follow Me, deny yourself, take up your cross daily, and follow.
Whoever wants to save their life will lose it. Whoever loses their life for My sake will save it.
What good is it to gain the world but lose yourself?
If you’re ashamed of Me and My words, I’ll be ashamed of you when I return in glory.
Some standing here won’t taste death till they see God’s kingdom.”
About eight days later, He took Peter, John, and James up a mountain to pray.
As He prayed, His face changed, His clothes flashed like lightning.
Two men appeared—Moses and Elijah—talking with Him.
They spoke about His upcoming departure in Jerusalem.
Peter and the others were half-asleep. When they woke up, they saw His glory and the two men.
As they were leaving, Peter said: “Master, it’s good we’re here. Let’s make three tents—one for You, one for Moses, one for Elijah.” He didn’t know what he was saying.
A cloud came and covered them. They were scared.
A voice from the cloud said: “This is My Son, My Chosen One. Listen to Him.”
When the voice stopped, Jesus was alone. They kept silent and told no one what they saw.
The next day, they came down the mountain. A big crowd met them.
A man shouted: “Teacher, look at my son—he’s my only child.
A spirit seizes him, he screams, convulses, foams. It barely leaves him.
I begged Your disciples to cast it out, but they couldn’t.”
Jesus said: “O faithless, twisted generation, how long must I deal with you? Bring your son.”
As the boy came, the demon slammed him down. Jesus rebuked it, healed the boy, gave him back to his father.
Everyone was amazed at God’s power.
While they were still marveling, He said to His disciples: “Let these words sink in: The Son of Man will be betrayed.”
They didn’t understand—it was hidden from them. They were afraid to ask.
A debate started among them—who was the greatest?
Jesus knew their thoughts. He took a child, stood him by His side,
and said: “Whoever receives this child in My name receives Me. And whoever receives Me receives the One who sent Me. The least among you is the greatest.”
John said: “Master, we saw someone casting out demons in Your name. We tried to stop him—he’s not with us.”
Jesus said: “Don’t stop him. If he’s not against you, he’s for you.”
When the time came for Him to be taken up, He set His face toward Jerusalem.
He sent messengers ahead. They entered a Samaritan village to prep for Him.
But the people didn’t welcome Him—He was headed to Jerusalem.
James and John said: “Lord, want us to call fire down from heaven on them?”
He turned and rebuked them.
They went to another village.
As they walked, someone said: “I’ll follow You wherever You go.”
Jesus said: “Foxes have dens, birds have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay His head.”
He said to another: “Follow Me.” The man said: “Let me bury my father first.”
Jesus said: “Let the dead bury their dead. You go preach God’s kingdom.”
Another said: “I’ll follow You, Lord, but let me say goodbye to my family.”
Jesus said: “No one who puts hand to plow and looks back is fit for God’s kingdom.”
After that, Jesus picked 70 more and sent them out in pairs to every place He planned to visit.
He told them, “The harvest is huge but the workers are few—pray for more people to step up.”
“Now go. I’m sending you out like sheep into a pack of wolves.”
“Don’t bring a bag, cash, or extra shoes. Don’t stop to chat on the road.”
“When you enter a house, say, ‘Peace to this place.’”
“If someone peaceful lives there, your peace will rest on them. If not, it’ll bounce back to you.”
“Stay in that house, eat what they give you, and don’t house-hop.”
“If a town welcomes you, eat what they serve.”
“Heal the sick there and say, ‘God’s kingdom just pulled up on you.’”
“But if a town doesn’t welcome you, go out and say this…”
“‘Even the dust from your streets—we’re wiping it off. Just know God’s kingdom came close.’”
“I’m telling you, it’ll be easier for Sodom than for that town on judgment day.”
“Woe to you, Chorazin and Bethsaida! If Tyre and Sidon saw what you saw, they’d be in full repentance mode.”
“It’ll be easier for Tyre and Sidon than for you when judgment hits.”
“And you, Capernaum—don’t think you’re getting VIP access to heaven. You’re headed down.”
“Whoever listens to you listens to Me. Whoever rejects you rejects Me—and the One who sent Me.”
The 70 came back hyped: “Lord, even demons dipped when we used Your name!”
Jesus said, “I saw Satan fall like lightning from the sky.”
“I’ve given you power to stomp on snakes and scorpions—nothing can really hurt you.”
“But don’t flex about spirits obeying you. Be glad your names are written in heaven.”
Jesus got hyped in the Spirit and said, “Thank You, Father, for hiding this from the proud and showing it to the humble. That’s Your vibe.”
“Everything’s been handed to Me by My Father. Only He knows Me, and I reveal Him to whoever I choose.”
Then He told the disciples privately, “Y’all are blessed to see what you’re seeing.”
“Prophets and kings wanted to see and hear this—but they didn’t get to.”
A lawyer stood up to test Him: “Teacher, what do I gotta do to get eternal life?”
Jesus said, “What’s written in the law? How do you read it?”
He answered, “Love God with all you’ve got, and love your neighbor like yourself.”
Jesus said, “You nailed it. Do that and you’ll live.”
But the guy wanted to justify himself, so he asked, “Who counts as my neighbor?”
Jesus replied, “A man was traveling and got jumped, robbed, and left half-dead.”
“A priest came by, saw him, and crossed to the other side.”
“Then a Levite came, looked, and also passed by.”
“But a Samaritan came, saw him, and felt compassion.”
“He patched him up, poured oil and wine on the wounds, and took him to an inn.”
“Next day, he gave the innkeeper money and said, ‘Take care of him. I’ll cover the rest later.’”
“So who was the real neighbor to the man who got jumped?”
The lawyer said, “The one who showed mercy.” Jesus said, “Go do the same.”
As they traveled, Jesus entered a village where a woman named Martha welcomed Him.
She had a sister, Mary, who sat at Jesus’ feet and soaked in His words.
But Martha was stressed with chores and said, “Lord, don’t You care that I’m doing all the work? Tell her to help me.”
Jesus said, “Martha, Martha, you’re worried about too much.”
“Only one thing really matters. Mary chose it—and it won’t be taken from her.”
One day Jesus was praying, and when He finished, one of His guys said, “Teach us how to pray like John taught his crew.”
He said, “When you pray, say: ‘Father, Your name is holy. Bring Your kingdom.’”
“‘Give us our daily bread—just enough for today.’”
“‘Forgive us like we forgive others. Don’t let us fall into temptation.’”
Then He said, “Imagine you go to your friend’s house at midnight and say, ‘Bro, I need three loaves.’”
“‘A friend just showed up and I’ve got nothing to feed him.’”
“And your friend says, ‘Don’t bother me. The door’s locked and everyone’s asleep.’”
“Even if he won’t get up because you’re friends, he’ll do it if you keep knocking.”
“So I’m telling you—ask and you’ll get it, seek and you’ll find, knock and it’ll open.”
“Everyone who asks gets something, everyone who seeks finds, and everyone who knocks gets in.”
“If your kid asks for bread, would you hand him a rock?”
“Or if he asks for a fish, would you give him a snake?”
“If you, being flawed, know how to give good gifts, how much more will your Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask?”
Jesus cast out a mute demon. When it left, the man spoke, and the crowd was shook.
But some said, “He’s using demon power—Beelzebub—to cast out demons.”
Others tried to trap Him, asking for a sign from heaven.
Jesus knew what they were thinking and said, “A kingdom divided can’t stand.”
“If Satan’s fighting himself, how’s his kingdom gonna survive?”
“If I cast out demons by Beelzebub, who do your people use? Let them be your judges.”
“But if I’m casting them out by God’s power, then God’s kingdom is already here.”
“When a strong guy guards his house, his stuff’s safe.”
“But if someone stronger beats him, he takes the armor and divides the loot.”
“If you’re not with Me, you’re against Me. No neutral zone.”
“When an evil spirit leaves someone, it wanders looking for rest. If it finds none…”
“…it says, ‘I’ll go back to my old place.’”
“It returns, finds it clean and empty, and brings seven worse spirits. Now it’s worse than before.”
As Jesus spoke, a woman shouted, “Blessed is the mom who birthed and raised You!”
He said, “Actually, blessed are those who hear God’s word and live it out.”
As the crowd grew, He said, “This generation wants signs, but only Jonah’s sign will be given.”
“Just like Jonah was a sign to Nineveh, I’ll be a sign to this generation.”
“The Queen of the South will rise at judgment and call y’all out—she came for Solomon’s wisdom, and someone greater is here.”
“The people of Nineveh will rise too—they repented at Jonah’s words, and someone greater is here.”
“No one lights a lamp and hides it. You put it up so people can see.”
“Your eye is like a lamp. If it’s healthy, your whole body’s lit. If not, it’s dark.”
“So watch out—make sure your light isn’t actually darkness.”
“If your whole body’s full of light, with no dark spots, you’ll shine bright like a lamp.”
While Jesus was talking, a Pharisee invited Him to dinner. Jesus went and sat down.
The Pharisee was surprised Jesus didn’t wash first.
Jesus said, “You clean the outside of the cup, but inside you’re full of greed and wickedness.”
“You fools—didn’t God make both the outside and the inside?”
“Give generously from the heart, and everything will be clean for you.”
“Woe to you Pharisees! You tithe the tiniest things but ignore justice and love. Do both.”
“Woe to you! You love front-row seats and public praise.”
“You’re like unmarked graves—people walk over you and don’t even know.”
A lawyer said, “Teacher, you’re roasting us too.”
Jesus said, “Woe to you lawyers! You load people with rules but don’t lift a finger to help.”
“You build tombs for the prophets your ancestors killed.”
“You’re basically saying, ‘We agree with our ancestors—they killed the prophets, and we’ll build the tombs.’”
“That’s why God said, ‘I’ll send prophets and apostles, and y’all will reject them too.’”
“So this generation will answer for all the prophet blood spilled since the beginning.”
“From Abel to Zechariah—yes, this generation will be held accountable.”
“Woe to you lawyers! You took away the key to knowledge. You didn’t go in, and blocked others too.”
When He left, the scribes and Pharisees started pressing Him hard, trying to catch Him slipping.
They watched closely, hoping He’d say something they could use against Him.
While the crowd was packed like a concert, Jesus told His squad, “Watch out for Pharisee vibes—they’re all cap.”
“Everything hidden will get exposed. Secrets don’t stay secret forever.”
“What you whisper in DMs will be screenshotted to the group chat.”
“Don’t fear people who can only hurt your body. That’s all they got.”
“Fear the One who can end your life *and* your soul. Yeah, fear Him.”
“Aren’t five sparrows sold for two coins? God doesn’t forget even one.”
“He’s got your hair count on file. Don’t stress—you matter more than birds.”
“If you rep Me in public, I’ll rep you in heaven.”
“But if you ghost Me, I’ll ghost you in front of the angels.”
“You can talk wild about Me and still be forgiven, but don’t diss the Holy Spirit.”
“When you get dragged into court, don’t panic about what to say.”
“The Holy Spirit will give you the words right when you need them.”
Someone in the crowd yelled, “Tell my brother to split the inheritance!”
Jesus said, “Bro, I’m not your family lawyer.”
Then He said, “Watch out for greed. Life isn’t about flexing your stuff.”
He told a story: “A rich guy had a farm that popped off big time.”
“He thought, ‘Where do I even put all this grain?’”
“Then he said, ‘I’ll tear down my barns and build bigger ones.’”
“‘Then I’ll chill, eat good, and vibe for life.’”
“But God said, ‘You fool. Tonight’s your checkout. Who gets your stuff now?’”
“That’s what happens when you stack cash but forget God.”
Then Jesus told His squad, “Don’t stress about food or drip.”
“Life’s more than what you eat or wear.”
“Look at the birds—they don’t farm or save, but God feeds them. You’re worth more.”
“Worrying won’t make you taller or add time to your life.”
“If you can’t control the small stuff, why stress the big stuff?”
“Look at flowers—they don’t hustle, but they outdress Solomon.”
“If God dresses grass like that, He’s got you. Stop doubting.”
“Don’t obsess over what to eat or drink. Don’t spiral.”
“That’s what the world chases. Your Father knows what you need.”
“Chase God’s kingdom first, and the rest will follow.”
“Don’t be scared, little squad. God’s happy to give you the kingdom.”
“Sell your stuff, give to the needy, and stack treasure in heaven—it never crashes.”
“Where your treasure is, your heart’s GPS is locked in.”
“Stay ready. Keep your spiritual fit on and your light on.”
“Be like people waiting for their boss to come home—ready to open the door fast.”
“Blessed are the ones He finds ready. He’ll serve *them* dinner.”
“Even if He shows up late, if you’re ready, you’re blessed.”
“If a homeowner knew when a thief was coming, he’d stay up.”
“Same for you—be ready. The Son of Man shows up when you least expect it.”
Peter asked, “Is this just for us or for everyone?”
Jesus said, “Who’s the wise manager the boss can trust to run things right?”
“If the boss comes back and finds him doing great, that guy’s winning.”
“He’ll get promoted to run the whole operation.”
“But if he thinks, ‘The boss is late,’ and starts wildin’ out…”
“…the boss will show up unannounced and fire him on the spot.”
“If you knew what to do and didn’t do it, that’s a major consequence.”
“If you didn’t know, it’s still a consequence—just lighter. More knowledge = more responsibility.”
“I came to light a fire on earth. I’m ready for it to blaze.”
“But first, I’ve got a baptism to go through—and it’s heavy.”
“You think I came to bring peace? Nah, I came to divide.”
“From now on, families will be split—three against two, two against three.”
“Father vs. son, mother vs. daughter, in-laws beefing—it’s gonna get real.”
Then He told the crowd, “You can read the weather, right?”
“If the wind’s from the south, you know it’s gonna be hot.”
“So how can you read the sky but miss what’s happening spiritually?”
“Why can’t you figure out what’s right on your own?”
“If someone’s suing you, settle before court—or you’ll pay every cent.”
“You won’t get out till you’ve paid the last penny.”
Some folks told Jesus about Pilate mixing Galilean blood with their sacrifices—straight-up wild.
Jesus said, “You think those Galileans were worse sinners ‘cause that happened? Nah.”
“Unless y’all turn your lives around, same fate’s coming for you.”
“What about the 18 people crushed when that tower in Siloam fell? You think they were the worst in Jerusalem?”
“Nope. But again—if you don’t repent, you’re next.”
Then He dropped a parable: “A guy had a fig tree in his vineyard. He came looking for fruit—zero.”
So he told the gardener, ‘I’ve checked this tree for three years—still nothing. Cut it down. Why let it waste space?’
The gardener said, ‘Boss, give it one more year. I’ll dig around it, add some fertilizer—let me work with it.’
‘If it grows fruit, great. If not, then yeah, chop it.’”
One Sabbath, Jesus was teaching in a synagogue.
A woman was there—bent over for 18 years, couldn’t stand up straight.
Jesus saw her and said, “You’re free now.”
He touched her, and boom—she stood up straight and praised God.
The synagogue leader got salty ‘cause Jesus healed on the Sabbath. “Six days to work—come back then, not today!”
Jesus clapped back, “You hypocrites! Don’t y’all untie your ox or donkey on the Sabbath to give it water?”
“So this woman, a daughter of Abraham, bound by Satan for 18 years—shouldn’t she be set free today?”
That shut His haters up. The crowd? They were loving every second.
Then Jesus said, “What’s God’s kingdom like? Let me break it down.”
“It’s like a mustard seed—tiny at first, but it grows into a tree where birds chill.”
He asked again, “What else can I compare the kingdom to?”
“It’s like a woman who hid yeast in three batches of dough—next thing you know, the whole thing’s rising.”
Jesus kept moving through towns, teaching on His way to Jerusalem.
Someone asked, “Lord, will only a few people be saved?”
He said, “Try hard to get through the narrow door. Many will try, but won’t make it.”
“Once the door’s locked and you’re outside knocking, it’s too late.”
“You’ll say, ‘But we ate with You! You taught in our streets!’”
“But He’ll say, ‘I don’t know you. Back away, you shady people.’”
“There’ll be crying and teeth-grinding when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and the prophets in the kingdom—and you’re not in.”
“People will come from everywhere—north, south, east, west—and sit down at the kingdom table.”
“Some who seem last now will be first then. And some first now? Dead last.”
That same day, some Pharisees said, “Leave this place. Herod’s trying to kill You.”
Jesus said, “Tell that fox I’m busy casting out demons and healing. I’ll finish My work on schedule.”
“I’ve gotta keep moving. A prophet doesn’t just die anywhere—it’s always Jerusalem.”
“Jerusalem, Jerusalem—you kill prophets and stone the ones sent to you. I wanted to gather you like a hen with her chicks, but you weren’t down.”
“Now your house is left empty. And you won’t see Me again till you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in God’s name.’”
One Sabbath, Jesus went to eat at a top Pharisee’s house, and they were lowkey watching His every move.
Right in front of Him was a guy swollen up with dropsy.
Jesus asked the lawyers and Pharisees, “Is healing on the Sabbath legal or nah?”
They stayed silent. So He healed the guy and sent him on his way.
Then He said, “If your ox or donkey fell in a ditch on the Sabbath, wouldn’t you pull it out?”
They had zero comebacks.
Jesus noticed how people were scrambling for the best seats, so He dropped a parable.
“If you’re invited to a wedding, don’t grab the VIP seat. Someone more important might show up.”
“Then the host will tell you to move, and you’ll have to downgrade in front of everyone.”
“Instead, sit in the back. Then the host might say, ‘Come up front!’ That’s a flex.”
“If you hype yourself up, you’ll get humbled. But if you stay low, you’ll get lifted.”
Then He told the host, “When you throw a lunch or dinner, don’t just invite your rich friends or fam—they’ll just invite you back.”
“Instead, invite the poor, the disabled, the outcasts.”
“You’ll be blessed, ‘cause they can’t pay you back—but God will at the resurrection.”
One guy at the table said, “Blessed is the one who eats in God’s kingdom!”
Jesus said, “A man threw a huge dinner party and sent out invites.”
“When it was time, he told his servant, ‘Go tell the guests—dinner’s ready!’”
“But they all started making excuses. One said, ‘I just bought land—gotta go see it.’”
“Another said, ‘I bought five oxen—need to test-drive them.’”
“Another said, ‘I just got married. Can’t come.’”
“The servant came back and told the master. He got mad and said, ‘Go bring in the poor, the blind, the disabled—everyone.’”
“The servant said, ‘Done. Still got room.’”
“The master said, ‘Then hit the streets and alleys. Bring in whoever you find. Fill this place.’”
“‘None of those first-invited folks are getting a bite.’”
Big crowds were following Jesus. He turned and said,
“If you don’t love Me more than your fam—even your own life—you can’t be My disciple.”
“If you’re not carrying your cross, you’re not following Me.”
“If you wanna build a tower, don’t you first check if you’ve got the funds?”
“Otherwise, you’ll lay the foundation and run out of cash. People will clown you.”
“‘Look at this guy—started a project he couldn’t finish.’”
“Or if a king’s going to war, won’t he check if his 10K can beat the other guy’s 20K?”
“If not, he’ll send a peace squad before the fight even starts.”
“Same with you—if you’re not ready to give up everything, you can’t be My disciple.”
“Salt is great. But if it loses its flavor, what’s the point?”
“It’s not even good for dirt or compost. It just gets tossed. If you’re really listening—lock in.”
All the tax guys and known sinners were pulling up to hear Jesus talk.
The Pharisees and law nerds were big mad: “This guy hangs with sinners and even eats with them.”
So Jesus hit them with this parable:
“If you had 100 sheep and lost one, wouldn’t you leave the 99 in the field and go find the one that dipped?”
“And when you find it, you’d throw it on your shoulders, hyped.”
“Then you’d call your friends and neighbors like, ‘Let’s celebrate—I found my lost sheep!’”
“Same way, heaven throws a party when one sinner turns back—way more than for 99 who didn’t need to.”
“Or imagine a woman with 10 coins who loses one. She’ll flip the house, light a lamp, sweep every corner till she finds it.”
“And when she does, she texts the group chat: ‘Found it! Let’s gooo!’”
“That’s how the angels vibe when one sinner turns their life around.”
Then Jesus said, “There was this dad with two sons.”
“The younger one said, ‘Dad, run me my share of the inheritance now.’ So the dad split the assets.”
“Not long after, the younger son cashed out and dipped to a far-off place. He blew it all on wild living.”
“Then a famine hit, and he was broke and starving.”
“He got a job feeding pigs—lowest of the low.”
“He was so hungry he wanted to eat the pig food, but no one gave him anything.”
“He came to his senses and thought, ‘Even my dad’s workers eat better than this.’”
“‘I’ll go home and say, “Dad, I messed up—against heaven and you.”’”
“‘I’m not even worthy to be your son. Just let me be a hired worker.’”
“So he headed home. But while he was still far off, his dad saw him, ran to him, hugged him, and kissed him.”
“The son said, ‘Dad, I sinned against heaven and you. I’m not worthy to be your son.’”
“But the dad told the servants, ‘Quick! Bring the best fit, a ring, and fresh kicks.’”
“‘Fire up the grill—we’re throwing a feast. My son’s back!’”
“‘He was dead and now he’s alive. He was lost and now he’s found.’ And the party started.”
“Meanwhile, the older son was out working. He came home, heard music and dancing, and was like, ‘What’s going on?’”
“He asked a servant, who said, ‘Your brother’s back! Your dad’s throwing a party!’”
“But the older brother got salty and wouldn’t go in. His dad came out to talk.”
“He said, ‘I’ve been grinding for you all these years. Never disobeyed. No party for me though.’”
“‘But this dude wastes your money on wild living and you throw him a feast?’”
“The dad said, ‘Son, you’ve always been with me. Everything I have is yours.’”
“‘But we had to celebrate—your brother was dead and now he’s alive. Lost and now found.’”
“‘It was only right to throw a party and be glad—he was dead, now he’s alive again; lost, now found.’”
Jesus told His disciples, “There was a rich guy whose manager got exposed for wasting his money.”
“He called him in and said, ‘What’s this I’m hearing? Bring me the receipts—you’re fired.’”
“The manager thought, ‘What now? I’m not built for manual labor, and begging? Nah, that’s not me.’”
“‘I got it—I’ll do something so people will take me in when I’m jobless.’”
“So he called in everyone who owed his boss money. First guy: ‘How much you owe?’”
“He said, ‘A hundred jugs of oil.’ Manager said, ‘Quick—change it to fifty.’”
“Next guy owed a hundred measures of wheat. Manager said, ‘Make it eighty.’”
“The boss actually praised the manager for being slick. People of this world know how to hustle better than the righteous sometimes.”
“So I’m telling you—use your money wisely to make real friends. When it’s gone, you’ll have eternal connections.”
“If you’re faithful with little, you’ll be faithful with much. If you’re shady with little, you’ll be shady with much.”
“If you can’t be trusted with money, who’s gonna trust you with true riches?”
“And if you can’t handle what’s not yours, who’s giving you your own?”
“No one can serve two bosses. You’ll either love one and hate the other. You can’t serve both God and money.”
The Pharisees, who were money-lovers, heard all this and mocked Him.
Jesus said, “Y’all love to look holy in public, but God sees your hearts. What people hype up, God might call trash.”
“The law and prophets were until John. Since then, the kingdom’s been preached—and people are pressing in hard.”
“But not even the tiniest part of God’s law will drop until it’s all fulfilled.”
“If you divorce your spouse and marry someone else, that’s cheating. And marrying someone divorced? Same thing.”
“There was a rich man who lived in luxury every day—designer fits, five-star meals.”
“And a poor man named Lazarus lay at his gate, covered in sores.”
“He wanted scraps from the rich man’s table. Even dogs came and licked his wounds.”
“Lazarus died and got carried by angels to chill with Abraham. The rich man died too—and ended up in flames.”
“In torment, he looked up and saw Abraham far off, with Lazarus beside him.”
“He shouted, ‘Father Abraham! Have mercy! Send Lazarus to dip his finger in water and cool my tongue—I’m burning here!’”
“Abraham said, ‘Remember, you had it good in life. Lazarus didn’t. Now he’s comforted, and you’re not.’”
“‘Plus, there’s a huge gap between us—no crossing over, even if we wanted to.’”
“The man said, ‘Then please send him to my dad’s house—’”
“‘I’ve got five brothers. Warn them so they don’t end up here too.’”
“Abraham said, ‘They’ve got Moses and the prophets. Let them listen to that.’”
“‘But if someone comes back from the dead, they’ll listen!’”
“Abraham said, ‘If they won’t listen to Moses and the prophets, they won’t believe even if someone rises from the dead.’”
Jesus told His crew, “Offenses are gonna happen, but whoever causes them? That’s a walking red flag.”
“It’d be better to get deep-sixed with a boulder necklace than to make one of these little ones trip.”
“So stay alert. If your friend messes up, call it out. If they own it, forgive them.”
“Even if they mess up seven times in one day and say, ‘My bad’ each time—forgive them. Every time.”
The apostles said, “Lord, boost our faith stats.”
Jesus said, “If your faith was even mustard-seed small, you could tell a tree to uproot and dive into the sea—and it’d listen.”
“If you had a servant plowing or herding, would you say, ‘Come chill and eat’ right after work?”
“Nah, you’d say, ‘Fix my dinner, serve me, then you can eat.’”
“Do you thank the servant for doing what he’s supposed to? Didn’t think so.”
“Same with you—when you’ve done what’s expected, say, ‘We’re just doing our job.’”
On His way to Jerusalem, Jesus passed through the border zone of Samaria and Galilee.
He entered a village and ten guys with leprosy stood at a distance.
They yelled, “Jesus, Master! Help us out!”
He saw them and said, “Go show yourselves to the priests.” As they went, they realized—they were healed.
One of them, seeing he was healed, spun around, shouting praise to God.
He dropped to the ground at Jesus’ feet, thanking Him hard. He was a Samaritan.
Jesus said, “Weren’t there ten of y’all? Where’s the other nine?”
“Only this outsider came back to say thanks?”
Then He told the man, “Get up and go. Your faith made you whole.”
The Pharisees asked when God’s kingdom was dropping. Jesus said, “It’s not something you’ll spot with binoculars.”
“You won’t say, ‘Look, it’s over there!’ The kingdom’s already among you.”
Then He told His disciples, “You’ll wish you could see just one day of the Son of Man’s return—but you won’t.”
“People will say, ‘Look here!’ or ‘Look there!’ Don’t fall for it. Don’t chase.”
“When I return, it’ll be like lightning—flashing across the whole sky.”
“But first, I’ve got to suffer and get rejected by this generation.”
“When I come back, it’ll be like Noah’s days—people eating, drinking, marrying, business as usual…”
“…until the flood hit and wiped them all out.”
“Same with Lot’s time—eating, drinking, buying, selling, planting, building…”
“…then fire and brimstone dropped from the sky and ended it all.”
“That’s how it’ll be when the Son of Man shows up.”
“If you’re on the roof that day, don’t go back inside for your stuff. Just go.”
“Remember Lot’s wife.”
“If you try to save your life, you’ll lose it. Lose it for Me, and you’ll find it.”
“That night, two people will be in one bed—one taken, one left.”
“Two women grinding grain—one taken, one left.”
“Two guys in a field—one taken, one left.”
They asked, “Where, Lord?” He said, “Where the body is, the vultures gather.”
Jesus told them a story to show why they should always pray and never give up.
“There was a judge in a city who didn’t care about God or people.”
“A widow kept coming to him like, ‘Get justice for me against my enemy.’”
“At first he ignored her, but then he thought, ‘I don’t care about God or people…”
“‘…but this lady’s wearing me out. I’ll give her justice so she stops bugging me.’”
Jesus said, “Did you catch what the shady judge just said?”
“Now imagine how much faster God will help His chosen ones who cry out day and night.”
“He’ll come through quick. But when the Son of Man returns, will He even find faith on earth?”
Then He told a story for people who thought they were all that and looked down on others:
“Two guys went to pray—one a Pharisee, the other a tax guy.”
“The Pharisee stood tall and prayed, ‘God, I thank You I’m not like these other clowns—robbers, cheaters, or that tax guy.’”
“‘I fast twice a week and give a tenth of everything I get.’”
“But the tax guy stood far off, wouldn’t even look up. He beat his chest and said, ‘God, have mercy on me—I’m a mess.’”
“That guy went home right with God, not the Pharisee. If you hype yourself up, you’ll get humbled. Stay low, get lifted.”
People were bringing babies to Jesus so He could bless them. The disciples tried to shut it down.
But Jesus said, “Let the kids come. Don’t block them. God’s kingdom belongs to people like them.”
“If you don’t receive God’s kingdom like a child, you’re not getting in.”
A ruler asked Him, “Good Teacher, what do I need to do to get eternal life?”
Jesus said, “Why call Me good? Only God is truly good.”
“You know the commandments: Don’t cheat, kill, steal, lie, or disrespect your parents.”
The guy said, “I’ve kept all that since I was a kid.”
Jesus said, “One thing left—sell everything, give to the poor, and you’ll have treasure in heaven. Then come follow Me.”
The guy got sad—he was loaded.
Jesus saw it and said, “It’s tough for rich folks to enter God’s kingdom.”
“It’s easier to push a camel through a needle than for a rich person to get in.”
The people were like, “Then who can even be saved?”
Jesus said, “What’s impossible for people is possible with God.”
Peter said, “We left everything to follow You.”
Jesus said, “Anyone who left house, fam, or job for God’s kingdom…”
“…will get way more in this life—and eternal life in the next.”
Jesus pulled the Twelve aside and said, “We’re heading to Jerusalem. Everything written about Me is about to go down.”
“I’ll be handed over to the outsiders, mocked, disrespected, and spit on.”
“They’ll beat Me, kill Me, and on day three—I’m coming back.”
But they didn’t get it. It was like the meaning was locked.
As Jesus neared Jericho, a blind guy was begging by the road.
He heard a crowd and asked what was going on.
They told him, “Jesus of Nazareth is passing by.”
He shouted, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
People told him to chill, but he yelled louder, “Son of David, help me!”
Jesus stopped and said, “Bring him here.” When the man came close, Jesus asked,
“What do you want Me to do for you?” He said, “Lord, I want to see.”
Jesus said, “See again. Your faith healed you.”
Instantly, he could see. He followed Jesus, praising God. Everyone who saw it was hyped and gave God glory.
Jesus pulled up in Jericho, just passing through.
There was this short king named Zacchaeus—top tax guy, and yeah, he was stacked.
He wanted to see who Jesus was, but the crowd was deep and he was fun-sized.
So he sprinted ahead and climbed a sycamore tree like a whole squirrel to get a better view.
Jesus walked by, looked up, and said, “Zacchaeus, come down quick—I’m crashing at your place today.”
Zacchaeus slid down that tree like it was a fire pole and welcomed Jesus with full joy.
The crowd started whispering, “Ugh, He’s staying with *that* guy? A whole sinner?”
Zacchaeus stood up and said, “Lord, I’m giving away half my stuff to the poor. And if I scammed anyone, I’ll pay ‘em back four times.”
Jesus said, “Today salvation hit this house. Zac’s part of Abraham’s fam too.”
“I came to find the lost ones and bring ‘em back.”
Since people thought the kingdom was about to drop instantly, Jesus told a story to set it straight.
“A nobleman dipped to a far country to get crowned king and come back.”
“Before leaving, he gave ten servants a stack each and said, ‘Run it up till I return.’”
“But the locals hated him and sent a message like, ‘We don’t want this guy ruling us.’”
“He came back king anyway. Then he called the ten servants to see what they did with the money.”
“First guy said, ‘Boss, your one stack made ten.’”
“‘Well done,’ the king said. ‘You handled a little—now run ten cities.’”
“Second guy said, ‘Your one stack made five.’”
“‘Nice. You’re in charge of five cities,’ the king said.”
“Then one guy said, ‘Here’s your stack. I kept it wrapped up, didn’t touch it.’”
“‘I was scared. You’re strict—you collect where you didn’t even invest.’”
“The king said, ‘If you *knew* I was like that, why didn’t you at least put it in the bank and earn interest?’”
“‘You could’ve done *something* with it.’”
“Then he told the others, ‘Take his stack and give it to the guy with ten.’”
They said, ‘But he already has ten!’
“‘Exactly. If you use what you’ve got, you’ll get more. If you don’t, even that gets taken.’”
“‘And those haters who didn’t want me as king? Bring ‘em here and end them in front of me.’”
After that, Jesus kept it moving—heading up to Jerusalem.
When He got near Bethphage and Bethany, by the Mount of Olives, He sent two disciples ahead.
“Go to the next village. You’ll find a young donkey tied up—never ridden. Untie it and bring it here.”
“If anyone asks, just say, ‘The Lord needs it.’”
They went and found it just like He said.
As they were untying it, the owners said, “Why y’all taking our donkey?”
They said, “The Lord needs it.”
They brought it to Jesus, threw their jackets on it, and helped Him hop on.
As He rode, people laid their coats on the road like a red carpet.
When they hit the slope near the Mount of Olives, the whole squad started shouting praise—“God’s got the W!”
“Blessed is the King coming in God’s name! Peace in heaven! Glory up top!”
Some Pharisees said, “Teacher, tell your people to chill.”
Jesus said, “If they stay quiet, the rocks will start yelling.”
As He got closer and saw the city, He started crying over it.
“If only you knew what could bring peace—but now it’s hidden from you.”
“Days are coming when your enemies will trap you in, every side locked down.”
“They’ll crush you and your people. Not one stone left. ‘Cause you missed your moment.”
Jesus entered the temple and started flipping tables—shutting down the scammers.
He said, “It’s written: My house is for prayer. Y’all turned it into a scam hub.”
He taught daily in the temple. The top priests and law experts wanted Him gone.
But they couldn’t touch Him—‘cause the people were locked in on every word He dropped.
One day, Jesus was teaching in the temple, dropping gospel and healing hearts. The top priests, law experts, and elders rolled up.
They said, “Who gave you the authority to do all this? Who signed off on you?”
Jesus said, “I’ll ask you something first. Answer Me this…”
“John’s baptism—was it from heaven or just human hype?”
They huddled up: “If we say ‘heaven,’ He’ll ask why we didn’t believe John.”
“But if we say ‘just human,’ the crowd might riot—they all stan John as a prophet.”
So they said, “We don’t know.”
Jesus said, “Then I’m not telling you where My authority comes from either.”
Then He told the people a parable: “A man planted a vineyard, leased it to farmers, and dipped for a while.”
“At harvest time, he sent a servant to collect his share. They beat the guy and sent him back empty.”
“He sent another—same treatment. Disrespected and beat down.”
“Sent a third—this one they straight-up injured and kicked out.”
The owner said, “I’ll send my son. Surely they’ll respect him.”
But the farmers saw him and said, “That’s the heir! Let’s jump him and take the inheritance.”
So they dragged him out and killed him. Jesus asked, “What do you think the owner will do?”
“He’ll pull up, destroy those farmers, and give the vineyard to others.” The crowd gasped, “No way!”
Jesus looked at them and said, “Didn’t you read this verse? ‘The stone the builders rejected became the cornerstone.’”
“Whoever trips over that stone gets wrecked. And if it falls on you? You’re dust.”
The religious leaders knew He was talking about them and wanted to arrest Him—but the people had Him trending.
So they sent undercover ops to trap Him with His own words and hand Him over to the governor.
They said, “Teacher, we know You’re real and don’t play favorites. You teach God’s truth straight up.”
“So tell us—should we pay taxes to Caesar or nah?”
Jesus saw through the setup and said,
“Show Me a coin. Whose face is on it?” They said, “Caesar’s.”
He said, “Then give Caesar what’s his—and give God what’s God’s.”
They were stunned. Couldn’t trap Him. Just stood there speechless.
Then some Sadducees pulled up—they don’t believe in resurrection. They hit Him with this:
“Moses said if a man dies with no kids, his brother should marry the widow and raise a family for him.”
“So there were seven brothers. First one married a woman and died childless.”
“Then the second married her—same result.”
“Then the third. All seven married her. No kids.”
“Finally, the woman died too.”
“So in the resurrection, whose wife is she? All seven were married to her.”
Jesus said, “In this life, people marry and get married.”
“But in the next life—the resurrection squad—they don’t marry. They’re built different.”
“They can’t die anymore. They’re like angels. God’s kids. Resurrection certified.”
“Even Moses showed resurrection’s real—remember the burning bush? He called God the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
“He’s not the God of the dead, but of the living. They’re all alive to Him.”
Some law teachers said, “That was a bar, Teacher.”
After that, no one dared ask Him anything else.
Then Jesus said, “How can they say the Messiah is David’s son?”
“David himself said, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, sit at My right hand…’”
“‘…till I make Your enemies Your footstool.’”
“So if David calls Him ‘Lord,’ how’s He his son?”
While the crowd listened, Jesus told His disciples,
“Watch out for the flexy scribes—they love long robes, VIP seats, and public praise.”
“They rob widows while praying long prayers to look holy. Judgment’s gonna hit them hard.”
Jesus looked up and saw rich folks dropping fat stacks into the temple offering box.
Then He saw a poor widow toss in two tiny coins—basically pocket change.
He said, “Real talk: this widow gave more than all of them.”
“They gave from their leftovers. She gave everything she had.”
Some people were hyping up the temple’s glow-up—fancy stones, gold vibes, donation plaques.
Jesus said, “You see all this? It’s all getting leveled. Not one stone left standing.”
They asked, “Teacher, when’s this going down? Any signs we should watch for?”
He said, “Don’t get played. Many will come using My name, saying, ‘I’m the one!’ Don’t follow them.”
“You’ll hear about wars and chaos—don’t freak out. That stuff has to happen first, but it’s not the end yet.”
Then He said, “Nations will beef with nations. Kingdoms will clash.”
“There’ll be earthquakes, famines, plagues. Wild stuff in the sky and on earth.”
“But before all that, they’ll come for you—arrests, hate, trials. Synagogues, prisons, kings, governors—all ‘cause you ride with Me.”
“That’ll be your moment to testify. Don’t waste it.”
“Don’t stress about prepping your speech.”
“I’ll give you words and wisdom they can’t argue with.”
“Even your fam—parents, siblings, cousins, besties—some will betray you.”
“You’ll be hated by everyone ‘cause of Me.”
“But not a single hair on your head will be wasted.”
“Stand firm, and you’ll secure your soul.”
“When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, know it’s about to get wrecked.”
“If you’re in Judea, run to the hills. If you’re in the city, get out. Don’t go back in.”
“Those will be days of justice—everything written will hit.”
“It’ll be brutal—especially for pregnant women and nursing moms. The wrath will be real.”
“People will fall by the sword, get taken captive. Jerusalem will be trampled by outsiders until their time’s up.”
“There’ll be signs in the sun, moon, and stars. Earth will be in panic—waves crashing, nations shook.”
“People will faint from fear, seeing what’s coming. The sky itself will be glitching.”
“Then they’ll see the Son of Man coming in power and glory, riding the clouds.”
“When this starts happening, stand tall—your rescue mission is close.”
He told them a parable: “Look at the fig tree—or any tree.”
“When the leaves pop out, you know summer’s near.”
“Same way, when you see these signs, know God’s kingdom is loading.”
“This generation won’t pass till all this happens.”
“Heaven and earth might pass, but My words? Locked forever.”
“Watch yourselves—don’t get caught slippin’ with partying, stress, or distractions. Don’t let that day sneak up on you.”
“It’ll hit everyone on earth like a trap.”
“Stay woke. Pray always. Be ready to escape what’s coming and stand before the Son of Man.”
Jesus taught in the temple by day, and at night He camped out on the Mount of Olives.
Every morning, the people pulled up early to hear Him drop truth in the temple.
The Passover festival, aka Feast of Unleavened Bread, was coming up.
The top priests were plotting how to cancel Jesus without causing a riot.
Then Satan slid into Judas Iscariot’s DMs—one of the Twelve.
Judas linked up with the priests and guards to plan how to hand Jesus over.
They were hyped and offered him a bag.
He agreed and started looking for the perfect no-crowd moment to betray Him.
Then came Passover kickoff—time to sacrifice the lamb.
Jesus said to Peter and John, “Go prep the Passover meal for us.”
They asked, “Where should we set it up?”
He said, “When you enter the city, you’ll see a guy carrying a water jug. Follow him.”
“Tell the homeowner, ‘The Teacher asks, where’s the room for the Passover with My crew?’”
“He’ll show you a big upstairs room. Set it up there.”
They went, found it just like He said, and got everything ready.
When it was time, Jesus sat down with the Twelve.
He said, “I’ve been waiting for this moment—to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.”
“I won’t eat it again till it’s fulfilled in God’s kingdom.”
He took a cup, gave thanks, and said, “Split this between y’all.”
“I won’t drink wine again till God’s kingdom shows up.”
Then He took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and said, “This is My body—given for you. Do this to remember Me.”
After dinner, He took the cup and said, “This cup is the new covenant—sealed in My blood, poured out for you.”
“But look—My betrayer’s hand is at this table with Me.”
“The Son of Man’s path is set, but woe to the one who sells Him out.”
The disciples started whispering, “Who’s gonna do it?”
Then they started beefing over who was the GOAT among them.
Jesus said, “Worldly rulers flex hard, calling themselves ‘benefactors.’”
“But not with you. The greatest should act like the youngest. The leader should serve.”
“Who’s greater—the one eating or the one serving? Normally the eater. But I’m here serving.”
“Y’all stuck with Me through the trials.”
“So I’m giving you kingdom rights—just like My Father gave Me.”
“You’ll eat and drink at My table in the kingdom and sit on thrones judging Israel’s twelve tribes.”
“Simon, Simon—Satan asked to sift y’all like wheat.”
“But I prayed for you, that your faith won’t fail. When you bounce back, strengthen your brothers.”
Peter said, “Lord, I’m ready to go to jail or die for You.”
Jesus said, “Peter, before the rooster crows, you’ll deny Me three times.”
Then He asked, “When I sent you out with no bag, cash, or extra shoes—did you lack anything?”
They said, “Nothing.” He said, “Now, take a bag. If you don’t have a sword, sell your hoodie and buy one.”
“Scripture says, ‘He was counted with the criminals.’ That’s about to happen.”
They said, “Lord, we’ve got two swords.” He said, “That’s enough.”
Jesus left and went to the Mount of Olives. The squad followed.
He told them, “Pray you don’t fall into temptation.”
He went a little farther, knelt down, and prayed,
“Father, if You’re willing, take this cup from Me. But not My will—Yours.”
An angel pulled up from heaven to give Him strength.
He was in deep agony—praying so hard He sweat blood.
He got up and found the disciples knocked out from sadness.
He said, “Why are y’all sleeping? Get up and pray so you don’t fall into temptation.”
While He was still talking, a crowd showed up. Judas led them and kissed Jesus to ID Him.
Jesus said, “Judas, you really betraying Me with a kiss?”
The disciples saw what was happening and said, “Lord, should we pull out the swords?”
One of them swung and sliced off the high priest’s servant’s ear.
Jesus said, “Enough!” Then He healed the guy’s ear.
He told the priests and guards, “Y’all came with swords and clubs like I’m some criminal?”
“I was with you daily in the temple—you didn’t touch Me. But this is your hour. Darkness gets its moment.”
They arrested Jesus and took Him to the high priest’s house. Peter followed from a distance.
They lit a fire in the courtyard. Peter sat down with them.
A servant girl saw him and said, “Hey, you were with Him!”
Peter said, “Nah, I don’t know Him.”
Later, someone else said, “You’re one of them.” Peter said, “Nope.”
About an hour later, another said, “He’s definitely with Him—he’s Galilean.”
Peter said, “Man, I don’t know what you’re talking about.” Right then, the rooster crowed.
Jesus turned and looked at Peter. Peter remembered what He said.
Peter dipped and cried hard.
The guards started mocking Jesus, beating Him up.
They blindfolded Him and said, “Prophesy! Who hit You?”
They kept roasting Him with all kinds of insults.
At daybreak, the council met and said, “If You’re the Messiah, tell us.”
He said, “If I tell you, you won’t believe Me.”
“And if I ask you questions, you won’t answer.”
“But from now on, the Son of Man will be seated at God’s right hand.”
They said, “So You’re the Son of God?” He said, “You said it.”
They said, “We don’t need more witnesses—we heard it from His own mouth.”
The whole squad got up and dragged Jesus to Pilate.
They said, “This guy’s out here twisting the nation, telling people not to pay taxes, and calling Himself a king.”
Pilate asked, “You the King of the Jews?” Jesus said, “You said it.”
Pilate told the priests and crowd, “I don’t see anything criminal here.”
But they kept pushing: “He’s stirring up chaos from Galilee to here!”
When Pilate heard “Galilee,” he was like, “Wait—is He under Herod’s jurisdiction?”
So he sent Jesus to Herod, who was in town.
Herod was hyped to see Jesus—he’d been hearing about Him and wanted to see a miracle.
He asked a bunch of questions, but Jesus said nothing.
The priests and law experts were there too, yelling accusations.
Herod and his squad mocked Jesus, dressed Him in a flashy robe, and sent Him back to Pilate.
That day, Herod and Pilate—who used to beef—became besties.
