Pilate called the priests, rulers, and crowd together.
“You brought this guy saying He’s causing trouble. I checked—He’s clean.”
“Herod checked too—same result. He’s done nothing death-worthy.”
“So I’ll rough Him up a bit and let Him go.”
(He had to release one prisoner for the festival.)
But the crowd yelled, “Cancel Him! Free Barabbas!”
(Barabbas was locked up for a riot and murder.)
Pilate tried again—he wanted to release Jesus.
But they shouted, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!”
A third time, Pilate said, “Why? What crime did He commit? I’ll punish Him and release Him.”
But they kept yelling louder: “Crucify Him!” The pressure was real.
So Pilate gave in and handed Jesus over.
He released Barabbas—the murderer—and gave them Jesus to do what they wanted.
As they led Jesus away, they grabbed a guy named Simon from Cyrene and made him carry the cross.
A crowd followed, including women crying loud.
Jesus turned and said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, don’t cry for Me. Cry for yourselves and your kids.”
“Days are coming when people will say, ‘Blessed are the childless.’”
“They’ll beg the mountains to fall on them and the hills to hide them.”
“If they do this when the tree’s green, imagine what happens when it’s dry.”
Two others—actual criminals—were also led out to be executed.
At the Skull spot, they crucified Jesus with the two criminals—one on each side.
Jesus said, “Father, forgive them. They don’t know what they’re doing.” The soldiers gambled for His clothes.
The crowd watched. Leaders mocked: “He saved others—can’t save Himself? If He’s God’s Chosen, let Him prove it.”
Soldiers mocked too, offering Him sour wine.
“If You’re the King of the Jews, save Yourself!”
A sign above Him said, “This is the King of the Jews.”
One criminal mocked Him: “Aren’t You the Messiah? Save Yourself—and us!”
But the other snapped back, “Don’t you fear God? We’re getting what we deserve.”
“But this guy? He did nothing wrong.”
Then he said, “Jesus, remember me when You hit Your kingdom.”
Jesus said, “Today you’ll be with Me in paradise.”
Around noon, darkness hit the land for three hours.
The sun dipped. The temple curtain tore in two.
Jesus shouted, “Father, into Your hands I give My spirit.” Then He breathed His last.
The Roman officer saw it all and said, “This man was truly innocent.”
The crowd saw what happened and left, beating their chests.
Jesus’ friends and the women who followed Him stood at a distance, watching.
A man named Joseph from Arimathaea—a good dude, part of the council—
(He hadn’t agreed with the others. He was waiting for God’s kingdom.)
He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body.
He took it down, wrapped it in linen, and laid it in a tomb cut from rock—brand new, never used.
It was Friday, almost Sabbath time.
The women who came with Jesus from Galilee followed and saw the tomb and how His body was placed.
They went home, prepped spices and perfumes, then rested on the Sabbath as the law required.
Early Sunday morning, the women pulled up to the tomb with the spices they prepped.
They found the stone rolled away—tomb wide open.
They stepped in and boom—Jesus’ body was gone.
While they were still shook, two men in drip so bright it blinded them showed up.
The women dropped to the ground, terrified. The men said, “Why you looking for the living in a graveyard?”
“He’s not here—He’s risen. Remember what He told you back in Galilee?”
“‘The Son of Man would be handed over, crucified, and rise on day three.’”
Then it clicked—they remembered His words.
They ran back and told the Eleven and the rest what happened.
It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary mother of James, and others with them.
But the guys thought it sounded like fanfic—didn’t believe it.
Peter ran to the tomb, peeked in, saw the linen wraps, and dipped—mind blown.
That same day, two of them were walking to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles out.
They were deep in convo about everything that went down.
As they talked, Jesus Himself pulled up and started walking with them.
But they didn’t recognize Him—eyes on lockdown.
He said, “What are y’all talking about that’s got you looking so down?”
One named Cleopas said, “You the only one in Jerusalem who missed what just happened?”
Jesus said, “What happened?” They said, “About Jesus of Nazareth—a prophet with power, words and works.”
“Our leaders handed Him over. He got crucified.”
“We were hoping He was the one to redeem Israel. It’s day three since it all went down.”
“Some women from our squad shocked us—they went to the tomb early…”
“…didn’t find His body, but said angels told them He’s alive.”
“Some of our guys checked—it was just like the women said. But no Jesus.”
Jesus said, “Y’all are slow to believe. Didn’t the prophets say this had to happen?”
“That the Messiah had to suffer before entering glory?”
Then He gave them the ultimate Bible study—starting from Moses through all the prophets, showing how it all pointed to Him.
They got near the village. Jesus acted like He was gonna keep walking.
But they said, “Stay with us—it’s late.” So He went in with them.
At dinner, He took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them.
Boom—their eyes opened. They recognized Him. Then He vanished.
They said, “Didn’t our hearts burn when He talked and broke down the Scriptures?”
They got up that moment and sprinted back to Jerusalem. Found the Eleven and others gathered.
The crew said, “It’s true! The Lord’s risen—He appeared to Simon!”
Then the two told their story—how they met Him on the road and recognized Him when He broke the bread.
While they were still talking, Jesus popped up in the room and said, “Peace, fam.”
They freaked out—thought they were seeing a ghost.
He said, “Why y’all trippin’? Why the doubt?”
“Look at My hands and feet—it’s Me. Touch Me. Ghosts don’t have flesh and bones.”
He showed them His hands and feet.
They were still in shock—too much joy to process. So He said, “Y’all got anything to eat?”
They gave Him some broiled fish—and a honeycomb.
He took it and ate it in front of them.
Then He said, “This is what I told you before—everything written about Me in the Law, Prophets, and Psalms had to happen.”
Then He unlocked their minds to understand the Scriptures.
He said, “It was written: the Messiah had to suffer, rise on day three…”
“…and repentance and forgiveness would be preached in His name to all nations—starting in Jerusalem.”
“Y’all are the witnesses of this.”
“I’m sending what My Father promised. Stay in the city till you’re powered up from heaven.”
He led them out to Bethany, lifted His hands, and blessed them.
While blessing them, He ascended—lifted off into heaven.
They worshiped Him, then went back to Jerusalem hyped.
They stayed in the temple nonstop, praising God.
